newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran urges Turkey to pull troops from north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges Turkey to pull troops from north Iraq.

text.p: Iran on Sunday called on Turkey to immediately pull its troops out of northern Iraq, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
The agency quoted Iranian deputy foreign minister for Asia-Pacific affairs Alaeddin Bourujerdi as saying: "The move taken by Turkey is not the solution to the problem".
"He urged Turkey to immediately bring the current situation in northern Iraq to an end," IRNA quoted him as telling a news conference.
Thousands of Turkish troops backed by air power poured into the region on May 14 in a cross-border operation against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) bases used for raids into southeast Turkey.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Sunday said the Turkish army's 25-day-old operation in northern Iraq was coming to an end.
Iran has denied Turkish charges it has given military assistance to PKK rebels fighting for independence or autonomy in southeastern Turkey.
"Bourujerdi once more stressed that Islamic Iran will continue to strictly follow its policy of not allowing the presence of the PKK forces on Iranian soil," IRNA said.
